How Seedance 2.5 pricing works

Seedance 2.5 pricing is based on input type, resolution (480p, 720p, or 1080p), aspect ratio, and video duration (4–30 seconds). You pay a per-second rate for the seconds of video the model processes.

There are two input modes, and they bill on different amounts of video:

  • •Text / Image-to-video: generate from a text prompt, a first-frame image, and/or reference images. You are billed for the video you generate. Text prompts and still images do not add a meaningful amount.
  • •Video-to-video: generate using one or more reference videos. You are billed for the video you generate plus the reference video the model reads. Every reference video counts, and their lengths add up. See the video-to-video section below before you budget.

Text / Image-to-video: Per-Second Rates

Multiply by your clip duration to get the total cost. These rates are per second of generated output.

Video-to-video: Per-Second Rates

Important: video-to-video bills your reference videos as well as your output. The rate below is lower per second than text / image-to-video, but it applies to more seconds: your output plus your reference footage. Budget with:

billed seconds = output duration + max(total reference duration, ⅔ × output duration, rounded up)
cost ≈ rate × billed seconds
  • •Total reference duration is the combined length of all reference videos you attach. Two references of 15s and 5s count as 20 seconds.
  • •There is a minimum. The reference portion is never billed at less than two-thirds of your output duration, rounded up to the next whole second (e.g. 3s for a 4s output, 7s for a 10s output, 20s for a 30s output). A reference shorter than that is billed at the minimum.
  • •There is no cap. Long references are billed at their full length.

This applies at every resolution, including 1080p. It is how the model bills, not a property of one tier.

Reference seconds are charged at the same per-second rate as your output (your output's resolution and aspect ratio), whatever the reference's own resolution or frame rate, so a lower-quality reference is not a cheaper one. A shorter one is, down to the minimum.

Is video-to-video cheaper than text / image-to-video? Usually not. With a reference as long as the output, video-to-video costs about 20% more than generating the same clip from text or an image. With a short reference (at or below the minimum), the two cost about the same.
